messages:
maria: heads-up — I ran an apples-to-apples comparison between the replay harness and the synthetic microbatch generator against the prefix/KV cache today. results look noisy under concurrent microbatching and kernel selection seems to correlate with hit-rate swings. attaching quick logs and numbers below. :thinking_face:

maria: command used:
```
./tools/replay_harness --trace=build/replays/customer_A.trace --concurrency=32 --microbatch=adaptive --seed=12345 --duration=10m --kv-mode=prefix
```

maria: short summary: replay hit_rate=82% (std=±7%), synthetic hit_rate=91% (std=±1%). p50 latency: replay=34ms, synthetic=29ms. p95: replay=210ms, synthetic=120ms. kernel-selection distribution from profiler looks bi-modal.

ow the log snippet showing kernel choices and a few kv counters:
```
[rt-prof] kernel_choice=mini-k seq_len=64 count=812  mem_pressure=0.68
[rt-prof] kernel_choice=full-k seq_len=64 count=143 mem_pressure=0.88
[kv] prefix_hits=32871 prefix_misses=6872 warmup_inserts=9407 evictions=423
[kv] concurrent_prefetch_attempts=1123 prefill_races=27
```

maria: i'm worried there's a feedback loop: when the runtime picks a heavier kernel (full-k) we see higher mem_pressure -> more evictions -> lower hit rate -> more cold starts -> more kernel switches. want to validate methodology before digging deeper.

owen: useful find. first check that the batcher config is identical between the two harnesses (max_tokens, max_batch_size, batch_timeout). tiny differences in batch formation can change kernel picker heuristics. also try pinning kernel policy to deterministic to see if variance disappears:
```
./tools/replay_harness --kernel-policy=deterministic --kernel-default=mini-k ...
```

owen: cc @maria also run with --kv-debug to get per-prefix timestamps (helps see the prefill races).

lee: another angle — concurrency can create hot-churn during warmup where N threads all try to prefetch the same prefix; that spiky insert pattern can thrash the cache even if absolute traffic is the same. to rule that out run a serialized prefill to warm the cache and then replay traffic:
```
./tools/replay_harness --preload-mode=serial --preload-threads=1 --preload-duration=5m --then-replay
```

anya: thanks. also confirm the synthetic generator is actually matching the same sequence-length and prefix distribution. in previous experiments the synthetic sampler had a slightly longer tail which favors mini-k (shorter kernels) and yields better hit rates. run with explicit seq_len-distribution file to force parity.

jay: putting a tiny checklist to get apples-to-apples:
- identical batcher flags
- same seq_len distribution (use --seq-dist-file)
- same kernel-policy or explicit kernel pinning
- identical kv capacity & eviction policy settings
- run with same RNG seed for synthetic

jay: here's a small helper I use to diff runs (very lightweight):
```
python tools/compare_runs.py --left run_replay.json --right run_synth.json --metrics kv_hit_rate p50 p95 kernel_counts
```

jay: expected output is a normalized table but for quick sanity check just compare kernel_counts: e.g., mini-k=820 vs mini-k=810 (close) but full-k diverging 140 vs 12 (huge).

simon: perf-bot posted an automatic trace for the failing run. fyi it also flagged a small regression in kernel-picker heuristic (PR: #3421) that landed last week — might be related. excerpt from perf-bot dump:
```
perf-bot: run=1955550002 mode=replay microbatch=adaptive kernel_picker_version=v3.4.1->v3.5.0
perf-bot: kernel_counts: {"mini-k":812, "full-k":143}
perf-bot: kv: hits=32871 misses=6872 evictions=423 warmup_time_s=73
```

maria: good catch on the PR. if we suspect the kernel-picker change, we should re-run with the previous kernel_picker_version pinned to verify. also Owen's suggestion to run with kernel-policy=deterministic will help isolate.

own: for concurrency-correctness, also enable the metrics that count 'duplicate-prefill' — that shows how often multiple workers raced to insert the same prefix and potentially caused eviction churn. flag is --kv-prefill-tracing.

anya: one more thought — quantify sensitivity by varying concurrency from 4->64 in steps and plotting kv_hit_rate vs kernel_choice_ratio. that usually shows whether the phenomenon is load-dependent or a pure heuristic bug.

jay: i can run a sweep tomorrow. plan: 4,8,16,32,64 threads, 10m each, collect kernel traces, kv evictions, and batch-size histogram. will attach runs to the compare script.

simon: created a perf ticket: INF-1192 with links to runs and perf-bot traces. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.

maria: action items agreed:
- jay: run concurrency sweep and produce normalized compare (jay will run overnight)
- owen: re-run with kernel_picker pinned & deterministic kernel-policy
- lee: run serialized prefill then replay (to measure warm vs cold)
- anya: verify synthetic generator seq_len and prefix distribution parity
- simon: collect perf-bot traces and link INF-1192 to the PR #3421

maria: if results still show variance after these controls we'll open a focused repro with an isolated microbenchmark that reproduces the kernel->eviction feedback. thanks all :thumbsup:
